title: Arkret Actor Profile Operations
description: Authorized anti-enumeration display view of a co-member global Actor Profile, served by the authenticated own Station. The ordinary profile Event is provenance, not a complete CRDT proof. The operation grants no identity, capability or membership authority and never requires an Event to obtain RealmCommit coverage.

resolve_request.description: Resolves current global Actor Profiles for actors the caller currently shares realm_id with. The caller MUST be an effective joined member of realm_id and every returned actor MUST also be one at evaluation time; realm_id is the authorization basis, not a display hint.

realm_id.description: Shared Collaboration Realm establishing the relationship. A Principal Control Realm MUST NOT be used here: PCR co-membership is the owner's own devices and would make this operation a self-read with an outward shape.

profile_event.description: The exact eligible profile Event that is the source of the deterministic current display projection. It is provenance only: retained losing writes and patch ancestry are not proven complete by this one Event. The service must return profile_unavailable if no eligible and disclosable source Event exists. Its Realm is the owner PCR; this limited disclosure never permits other PCR Events.

resolved_actor_profile.description: One actor display projection from the authenticated own Station and the exact accepted profile Event sourcing its deterministic current value. The Station validates ordinary eligibility and causal reduction before serving it. A single patch Event does not prove the full retained evidence set, patch ancestry, historical completeness or global freshness. An independent verifier needs the complete authorized causal/evidence closure; this DTO makes no such proof claim. Neither field is a grant, selector authority or identity-resolution authority. Ordinary profile Events have no covering RealmCommit.

resolve_failure.description: Per-actor failure. The reason vocabulary is deliberately single-valued: unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, actor that is not an effective joined member of realm_id, and a caller not authorized for that actor MUST all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot be used to probe membership or account existence.

resolve_outcome.description: Closed outcome. Every requested actor_id appears exactly once across profiles and failures, so a caller cannot distinguish an omitted actor from a withheld one.

account_status_projection.description: Optional AccountStatusRecord projection served beside the profile. The durable Actor Profile object used to carry a status member, which was unwritable by construction: zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 keeps AccountStatusRecord out of every authority stream, RealmCommit, Control Proposal and reducer, so no registered result_writes[] row could ever produce it and no author could be allowed to. It is a read-side projection and lives here. The Station MUST have verified the exact record it is projecting -- the same account_id, the record's own proof, and the status_seq against its durable monotonic replica head -- and MUST omit this member entirely when it holds no verified record. Omission means unknown. A caller MUST NOT read a missing member as active, and MUST NOT cache a status across a profile revision: the record changes on the Account Authority's clock, not on the profile's.

status.description: The closed AccountStatusRecord lifecycle value of zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3. Implementations MAY coarsen or withhold the projection, but MUST NOT invent a value.

status_seq.description: status_seq of the exact record projected, so the caller can order and re-check it.
